newsitem.title: BURMA: Suu Kyi says to hold meetings as barriers removed.
newsitem.headline: Suu Kyi says to hold meetings as barriers removed.

text.p: Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi responded to the military's removal of checkpoints barring access to her house by saying she was ready to resume her recently aborted weekly public gatherings.

"A few blockades do not constitute obstacles to democratisation. We shall have to meet as long as people desire to meet. Come and see," Suu Kyi told a news conference hours after the checkpoints were removed, when asked if she would hold her weekly public meetings again.

The checkpoints were set up on September 26 to prevent Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) from holding a party congress from September 27-29. But they also stopped her from holding her public gathering on weekends usually attended by thousands of supporters.
The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) also detained 573 NLD members and supporters in a subsequent crackdown. All but 63 have since been released.
"What the SLORC did during the past 10 days did not damage the NLD. But they were illegal processes that damaged the reputation of the SLORC," Suu Kyi said.

When asked if she supported a recent U.S. ban on travel visas for some senior Burmese leaders and their families, she said: "We support all actions that that are intended to help in democractisation." The SLORC responded to the U.S. ban by banning visas for certain categories of American citizens.
